item.title: {tor,mullvad}-browser: 15.0.26 -> 16.0
item.description:
blog: https://blog.torproject.org/new-release-tor-browser-160/ (if it's not here yet, it will be once https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/web/blog/-/merge_requests/642 is merged) tb changelog: https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/applications/tor-browser-build/-/raw/tbb-16.0-build1/projects/browser/Bundle-Data/Docs-TBB/ChangeLog.txt mb changelog: https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/applications/tor-browser-build/-/raw/mb-16.0-build1/projects/browser/Bundle-Data/Docs-MB/ChangeLog.txt firefox esr: https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/153.6.0/releasenotes/ firefox security advisories: https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-120/

it's that time! this release notably brings us up to firefox 153 esr, as well as adding support for aarch64-linux.

Closes #491286. we've been able to build for aarch64-linux, and even launch the browsers in binfmt_misc with qemu-user, but not do any sort of meaningful wide-scale testing since we don't have a graphical aarch64-linux machine. cc @mio-19 @DaVinci42 @affhp, as folks who have expressed interest in aarch64-linux support before and may be able to test.

backporting note: we will have to backport this change. the tor project will no longer be supporting the tb/mb 15.0 release series, nor does upstream mozilla support 140 esr (it's been eol since 2026-09-29, though the tor project backported security fixes on their own last release). programs which need security updates like browsers have always been an exception to the major changes restrictions.

i haven't gotten in any deep testing of tor browser yet, only mullvad browser (though i have been testing TB alphas periodically). will try to get back to TB in a few hours, but anyone else feel free to do so in the interim. its rather unfortunate that the major version updates are tied up with security updates :upside_down_face:
